newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa hopes for trade deal with EU by April.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa hopes for trade deal with EU by April.

text.p: South Africa said on Monday it hoped to win approval for a protocol giving it partial membership of the Lome Convention in April.
A statement issued following weekend talks here with European Union trade officials said the two sides had found some common ground on an agreement which could benefit both their export industries.

"The government of South Africa expressed the hope that the ACP/EU Council of Ministers will be able to approve this protocol at its meeting of the 24th and 25th of April in Luxembourg," the statement said.

The EU has rejected post-apartheid South Africa's demand for full accession to the Lome Convention, which grants favourable access to EU markets to developing countries elsewhere in Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific (ACP).

But the joint statement said both sides had agreed that the EU would generally be prepared to open its markets faster and more extensively for South African products than it will ask South African to do for EU products.
Further South Africa/EU trade talks will be held in Brussels next month.
